items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Chris did have bad shoes... Chris was a man that's not like to drink... I wouldn't play with Chris, man.

ctx.x: Broken shoes. Oh, I wouldn't say that. No, I wouldn't. No, I wouldn't do that. No, I wouldn't do that.

Chris did have bad shoes. With that question, Doc, he sure did. Because when Faye saw that time, him and Black Banner had that humbug about tuxedo suits and all that. Chris was a man that's not like to drink, you know. He was a good blues man and didn't wear too much fancy clothes, you know. No, no. That's why we tell the people the truth.
But now, Celestan and Pirone's band, you played with them. Yeah, them guys were uniform. What were they dressed like?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: Oh, me and Chris come from the same home. He got on the Chris all my life.

ctx.x: Who did he play with down there?
He played with Mike Gouldie band. Uh huh. Mike Gouldie band. And uh, Harrison Bones, Pierre Anderson. He left the country and played with all the different bands. Chris Kelly.
Who did Pierre Anderson play with? I don't know about him.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: I always remember Chris's band... I'd go play... In his place, of course, for a week... I'd work Sunday in his place

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Well, who did you play with when you started playing?

Oh, I played with, I played with a lot of bands. One of the team and brass bands, Kid Rene, Chris Kelly, Kid Punch. Yeah, play with the, play with the record. I don't play with the exhausts, no, I don't play with them. I was playing, I didn't play good like that. Tuxedo.
What would've, say Buddy Petite's brass band, what numbers would they feature?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: Oh, me and Chris come from the same home. He got on the Chris all my life.

ctx.x: What about Chris Kelly? How long you know him?

Oh, me and Chris come from the same home. He got on the Chris all my life. You know, I was like, Christmas. Older than what I was, Christmas was my brother Sam. He was there. How old would Sam be? My brother Sam would be, he said it would be 73 other days. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. A couple years older than you. Yeah, 73 other days. Christmas, same age with him. Well, Chris died pretty young. Chris died in, Chris died in, Chris died in, I tell you that Chris died in 28, 1928. When, when, when, when she called, we put the…
About 1888. He wasn't old married with him. About 1888. About 1888. About 1888. About 1888. About 1888.
